correctness.rationale: The deficiency sum for an n-coloring permits at most one singleton. Except at at most two vertices, the code is therefore determined by its one missing color, giving a contradiction for n>=3. The proposed proper (n+1)-coloring distinguishes the incident-color complements, which are exactly the nonzero coordinates of the locating codes. I checked the terminal-versus-bulk congruences, the complete four-collision list in the divisible-by-three case, and the replacement pairs including k=3 and k=4. The three small permutations work. Unused colors are ruled out by the number of distinct two-element complements.
residual_risks: The replay is finite corroboration; the arithmetic case argument covers all orders in the claim. No scope extension to n=4,5.
